tells: Gestural, dry-brush painted frames: visible bristle drag and opacity build-up. Nothing looks like vector defaults.
The aspect ratio changes from frame to frame (tall portrait, near-square, landscape). That reads as a deliberate formal device, as if the frame itself is being animated.

A specific city/transit idea: an Art Deco spire becomes a subway window with a passenger, then a striped grid, then crossing tracks, then a yellow route line, then a map-like grid. Each shot is built from the brushstrokes of the one before.
The primary palette (cobalt, cadmium yellow, red, green, black, white) is restrained and committed, with a Bauhaus/Matisse echo, and doesn't look like a template accent colour.
No type. That serves the piece: the image carries the whole narrative, and type would flatten its painterly rhythm.
gaps: Some middle frames (crossed white strokes, yellow route) are close to pure abstraction. Anchor them with one more figurative beat so the story survives a still read.
Finish is uneven: some edges and fills look like quick sketch passes next to more resolved frames like the subway window. Settle on one level of finish.
A closing frame that brings the city, the figure and the grid together would turn a strong sequence into a memorable ending.

tells: Rich material finish: the oxblood ground has a woven/twill texture, there is halftone and grain on the animals, and soft cut-paper drop shadows give each object physical presence.

An unusual, disciplined palette of deep red with slate teal, ochre and cream, held across every frame.

gaps: The structure is one centred hero object on the same wallpaper, six times. The choreography reads as a carousel, so the objects need to interact, collide or transform into each other.
No camera or scale variation (no close-ups, no wides, no layering of objects at depth). Vary the framing so every frame is a different poster.
The idea stays decorative. Give it a narrative turn or reveal (the eyes in the flowers are the seed of one) so it is remembered and not just admired.

tells: The figures are drawn with real skill: rim-lit profiles, freckles, the headphone figure sinking into a pillow. The light is motivated and glows from within.

On the other side, two of the six frames are effectively blurred gradient blobs (mirrored ripple, concentric portal), and the glass star reads like a stock-3D/glassmorphism trope.
The 'wellness app' pastel blue-peach palette is very familiar territory. No type is visible, which is neutral here.
gaps: Replace the gradient-portal interludes with designed transitions that carry a subject. As they stand they are effect without content.
Push the palette and idea away from the meditation-app house style toward something only this piece could be.
Add texture or grain variation and stronger compositional contrast (scale, cropping, negative space) so the frames stop blending into one airbrushed haze.

defects: Fill shapes on the bergamot, the peach and the target in the opening topo are revealed by a radial wedge sweep. Mid-transition they read as Pac-Man cutouts, with a hard edge, no feathering and no brush logic.

The colour fills sit visibly off-register from the line art (the bergamot's yellow spills outside the rind, the peach's orange shifts down-left). The offset is the same on every element, so it reads as a fixed offset, not hand-printed misregistration.
The bean grid builds in strict reading order, one bean at a time, with the same stroke-on and fill-wipe on each. It is a mechanical stagger with no variation in timing, scale or arc.
The 'Washed.' ring does nothing but drift and scale slightly across the brush stroke. It looks like a leftover cursor, not a designed element.
Type blocks and labels are static once on screen. Nothing animates out; each section is cleared or replaced rather than moved on by a transition.
The paper vignette has blotchy, low-frequency luminance patches (top right, centre) that look like noise-based shading, not a lit surface.
In both 1/6 s pairs the only change is an incremental reveal. There is no secondary motion, no overlap and no follow-through.
It is a single 20 s shot that steps through sections like slides. 12 of 19 seconds are nearly static.
gaps: Choreography: every beat is the same reveal-then-hold. Top studios link sections with match-moves (the topo rings could become the cup, the brush stroke could become water, the beans could become the final contour). They also vary tempo and use overlapping actions, with eased, weighted moves instead of linear wipes and sequential pops.

Sound: the bed is a dense, evenly loud loop of transients (~3 per second) at a constant level. It has one textural lift around 10.5 s and no dynamic arc. Hits are not tied to the section changes or reveals, and there are no designed foley cues (pour, rustle, roast crackle) that the illustrated subjects invite.

Finish: the hand-drawn concept is let down by procedural tells: hard-edged radial fill wipes, uniform misregistration, generic noise vignetting and identical per-instance animation. A top studio would hand-time the line boil, give the fills ink texture and reveal them with organic mattes.
